hooks_tab.title: Hooks
hooks_tab.description: Run a program or send an HTTP request chosen by the administrator when a user sends a message, before and after a tool runs, and when a reply ends. Hooks can only block or ask a person to confirm; they cannot allow anything. If a hook itself fails or times out it does not block, and the failure only shows in the run log, so do not rely on a hook as your only safeguard. Hook programs run with Touka's own permissions and no isolation, so only use programs you trust. Commands do not go through a shell. Scripts and any paths in the arguments must be in the hooks/ folder of the config folder; the program must be in hooks/ or somewhere agents cannot write to (for example the system interpreter). Anything else is refused. Do not use launchers such as env, npx or py, which look up the program to run on their own, and install the packages your scripts use inside hooks/ (for example hooks/node_modules) by copying them (for example set UV_LINK_MODE=copy for uv, or pass --package-import-method=copy to pnpm; npm copies already): uv and pnpm may share one copy of a file through hard links, so an agent changing the copy in its own project would also change the one your hook uses. On Linux and Docker, arguments cannot contain URLs (":" is treated as a path list separator); put URLs in a settings file inside hooks/ and have the script read it. Every user's conversations trigger hooks, incognito chats included, and the message and tool content is sent to them (the event is marked incognito; the hook decides whether to keep it). "When a user sends a message" only checks text sent in a chat; heartbeats, scheduled prompts and re-triggered runs do not trigger it, so it cannot be used to restrict users. "Before a tool runs" only covers calls made through the tool executor (the agent's tools and debug runs); task verification commands and trial runs do not trigger it. Extra context from tool hooks is added to the tool result, so the conversation's user can see it and it is saved with the conversation. When a program blocks with exit code 2, its standard error is shown to the conversation's user as the reason, so do not put secrets in it. HTTP hook replies must not be compressed; a compressed reply counts as a failure.

agent_reset.title: Agent Data Reset
agent_reset.intro: Reset one agent's accumulated runtime data (conversations, memory, stats, missions, outputs) back to a clean state. The agent's identity (soul / system prompt) and system audit trail are fully preserved, so it stays usable afterward. This is a destructive operation; a system backup is created first as a restore point.
agent_reset.confirm_body: This is irreversible. Review the scope below, type the agent ID, and re-enter your password to proceed.

scrub.option_label: Also clear this soul's memory from backups (off by default)
scrub.will_clear: This soul's memory (facts and semantic index) in the memory-store upgrade backups and in every system snapshot on the Settings backup list, including the one made just before this reset. When everything succeeds, no snapshot on the restore list can bring this soul's memory back.
scrub.wont_clear: Conversations in snapshots (anything said in a conversation stays in its history), the activity timeline, stats, missions, outputs; the legacy facts.jsonl; memory written under the old ID prefix (ToukaSoul…); backups that are not on the backup list (for example ones saved elsewhere from the command line); backups already downloaded; other souls' data; long-term memory (old conversations trimmed into the archive) is not cleared either.
scrub.guarantee: What is guaranteed: the memory can no longer be read from the memory store or backup files. This is not a forensic disk wipe. It needs a human admin signed in as themselves (not acting as another agent) who re-enters their password.
scrub.duration: With many snapshots this can take a few minutes.
scrub.acknowledge: I understand, clear the memory from backups
scrub.acknowledged: Confirmed: memory will also be cleared from backups
scrub.wipe_list: Conversations, memory, stats, missions, outputs, context snapshots; plus this soul's memory in upgrade backups and system snapshots
scrub.keep_list: Identity (soul / system prompt), archive, audit ledgers, uploaded files, conversations and other data in snapshots, other souls' memory, long-term memory (old conversations trimmed into the archive), the home folder of terminal commands (cleared only when the soul is deleted)
scrub.not_run: The server did not clear the backups: the memory in them is unchanged.
scrub.toast_incomplete: "{{id}}" was reset, but its memory was not cleared from every backup — see results
scrub.summary_complete: This soul's memory has been cleared from every snapshot on the backup list and every upgrade backup. It cannot be recovered.
scrub.summary_complete_out_of_scope: Within the clearing scope, this soul's memory has been cleared from every snapshot on the backup list and every upgrade backup. It cannot be recovered. Backups that still hold legacy-format or legacy-prefix memory outside the clearing scope (see the list below): {{n}}.
scrub.summary_unfinished: Clearing did not finish: {{reason}}. Backups may still contain this soul's memory; you can reset again with clearing turned on.
scrub.reason_see_details: some items were not cleared; see the details below
scrub.files_left: These {{failed}} files were left unchanged and still contain this soul's memory; the other {{done}} were cleared and cannot be recovered.
scrub.summary_not_ran: Clearing did not run ({{reason}}); the backups are unchanged.
scrub.live_verify_failed: The live memory store failed verification after compaction. Stop saving memory for now and contact the team.
scrub.live_not_compacted: The live memory store was not compacted ({{reason}}).
scrub.live_rewritten: This soul wrote new memory after the reset, so the live memory store holds its memory again.
scrub.remaining_unknown: Could not confirm whether anything remains in the live store.
scrub.remaining_positive: This soul wrote new memory after the reset, for example because its heartbeat is still running. Turn the heartbeat off, then try again.
scrub.collection_shared: This soul shares its semantic index with {{id}}. A normal reset works, but backups cannot be cleared.

reasons.in_use: the file is in use by another program
reasons.unreadable: the file could not be read
reasons.too_large: the file is too large to process
reasons.has_journal: the memory store has an unfinished write journal
reasons.unknown_schema: the memory store format is not recognized
reasons.unknown_qdrant_meta: the semantic index list is not recognized
reasons.collection_shared: the semantic index is shared with another ID
reasons.ambiguous_member: the backup has entries that differ only by letter case
reasons.changed_during_scrub: the file changed while it was being cleared
reasons.verify_failed: verification failed after clearing; the original was kept
reasons.live_verify_failed: the live memory store failed verification after compaction
reasons.rewritten_after_reset: this soul wrote new memory after the reset
reasons.list_failed: the file list could not be read
reasons.lock_timeout: timed out waiting for another operation
reasons.recheck_failed: could not recheck the live store
reasons.own_snapshot_missing: the snapshot made before this reset was not found
reasons.reset_not_clean: the reset was not fully clean, so nothing was cleared
reasons.out_of_scope: outside the clearing scope (legacy format or prefix)
reasons.write_failed: could not write the temporary file; the original was kept
reasons.own_snapshot_unverified: the snapshot made before this reset did not lose any memory, so it could not be confirmed as cleared
reasons.backup_failed: the snapshot before the reset could not be made, so nothing was cleared
reasons.cancelled: the request was cancelled before clearing started
reasons.os_metadata_file: a file the operating system put there (thumbnail cache or folder settings); it holds no memory and was left as it is

reasons.native_platform: Touka isn't running in Docker on Linux (for example, it runs directly on Windows), and this setup has no isolation.
reasons.probe_pending: Touka just started and is still checking whether isolation works, which usually takes a few seconds; you can reject now and try again shortly.
reasons.executor_unreachable: An isolation executor is configured but can't be reached right now (its container may not be running).
reasons.executor_runner_unavailable: The isolation executor isn't hooked up yet, so this can't be handed to it.
reasons.isolation_unavailable: Isolation isn't available right now, so this can't run isolated.
reasons.landlock_abi_too_old: The host's Linux kernel is too old (6.2 or newer is needed) and has no file isolation.
reasons.landlock_abi_insufficient: The host's Linux kernel isn't new enough (6.7 or newer is needed) to block connections to Touka's internal services, so isolation isn't complete.
reasons.selftest_failed: The isolation self-check failed, so Touka can't confirm isolation really works.
reasons.fs_9p: Touka's data sits on a disk isolation can't cover (for example a Windows disk mounted through Docker Desktop or WSL), and the isolation test there failed; Touka rechecks regularly.
reasons.net_tcp_fastopen:
TCP Fast Open is on, and isolation can't block connections opened with it. Add this to {{service}} in your compose file (or override):
sysctls:
  net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen: 0
then run (with the -f files you normally use):
docker compose up -d
If you run Touka directly on a Linux host without Docker, set net.ipv4.tcp_fastopen=0 on the host instead (see README_QUICKSTART).
reasons.net_mptcp:
The kernel has MPTCP turned on, and isolation can't block MPTCP connections. Add this to {{service}} in your compose override:
sysctls:
  net.mptcp.enabled: 0
then run (with the -f files you normally use):
docker compose up -d
If you run Touka directly on a Linux host without Docker, set net.mptcp.enabled=0 on the host instead (see README_QUICKSTART).
reasons.kernel_outdated:
The isolation code doesn't match the image (sandbox_kernel changed without a rebuild). Run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.kernel_not_installed:
The image is an old version without the isolation environment. Run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.kernel_changed: The isolation code changed after it was checked, so isolation can't be confirmed this time; Touka will recheck.
reasons.sandbox_state_unconfigured:
Touka's compose setup hasn't been updated yet (touka-sandbox-state is missing). Update compose following the upgrade steps, then run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.spec_too_large: Too many folders would be opened to this command, so the isolation settings exceed the limit and it can't run isolated.
reasons.scan_limit: This project is too large (or scanning took over 2 seconds) to confirm it holds none of Touka's files, so it can't run isolated.
reasons.protected_location: This project sits in one of Touka's protected locations (such as ToukaChat, scripts or .git), so it can't run isolated.
reasons.runner_not_wired: This tool isn't hooked up to isolation yet, so it can only run without isolation.
reasons.landlock_unavailable: This host's Linux kernel doesn't have Landlock (its file isolation feature) turned on, so nothing can be isolated.
reasons.isolation_check_failed: Something went wrong while checking isolation, so to be safe this run is treated as not isolated.
reasons.executor_auth_failed:
Touka reaches the executor but its access token doesn't match or can't be read (the executor just restarted with a new token, or a command changed the permissions of the executor's control channel; the executor fixes them every 5 seconds). This usually recovers within seconds; if it keeps happening, run:
docker compose restart touka-executor
reasons.executor_version_mismatch:
The executor and Touka are different versions (usually only one of them was rebuilt). Run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.executor_roots_mismatch:
The folders mounted in the executor differ from what Touka expects (the compose setup doesn't match). Update compose following the upgrade steps, then run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.executor_selftest_failed:
The executor's self-check failed, so Touka can't confirm its isolation really works. Run:
docker compose up -d --build
If that doesn't help, check the touka-executor log.
reasons.executor_restarted: The executor restarted before this command started, so it wasn't handed over; Touka will recheck, which usually takes a few seconds.
reasons.executor_rejected:
The executor refused this command (it and Touka disagree about this run's settings); Touka will recheck. If it keeps happening, run:
docker compose up -d --build
reasons.agent_dir_not_in_executor: This agent's folder isn't in the executor (for example custom models such as DebugAgent), so its commands can only run inside Touka's main container and each one needs your approval.
reasons.project_not_in_executor: This conversation is bound to a project, and the project folder isn't mounted in the executor, so every command needs your approval; with nobody present it is refused.
reasons.block_ports_incomplete: Touka can't read the custom connection settings (connections.json), or the file is broken, so it isn't sure which upstream ports to block. Once the file's content or permissions are fixed it recovers within about half a minute; if permissions need touka-init, follow the recovery steps in the upgrade guide (they already include a restart).
reasons.block_ports_overflow: More than 1024 ports would need blocking (too many upstream addresses in custom connections and MCP), so only Touka's own ports are blocked. Reduce the upstream addresses in custom connections or MCP, then restart Touka.
reasons.interpreter_untrusted:
The Python that Touka uses to start isolation isn't trusted: in a container, it (or a folder on its path) isn't owned by root or can be changed by someone else; running directly on a host, the Python behind the venv can't be found. So this can't run isolated. With Docker, rebuild the image:
docker compose up -d --build
Running directly on a Linux host, check where Python is installed (the Python the venv points to still exists and its path resolves).

sandbox_state_unconfigured.not_writable:
The isolation scratch area (touka-sandbox-state) has the wrong permissions, usually because an old image started first. To fix it:
1. docker compose down (without -v)
2. docker volume rm touka_touka-sandbox-state
3. docker compose up -d --build
(This only deletes caches and temporary files, not your data.)

Pausing this soul's heartbeat schedule first keeps it from running again between the reset and the delete.
